colorJourney.heroDescription: Primaries, secondaries and tertiaries — RYB theory and mixing recipes for drawing and painting.
colorJourney.wheelHint: Touch the wheel, then adjust the lightness

guidance.primarySubtitle: Choose your dominant primary colour — red, yellow or blue. This is the base of your painting palette.
guidance.primaryTheory: In painting (RYB model), the three primaries are not mixed into each other: they are the starting point for every other hue.
guidance.secondarySubtitle: Mix two primaries to get a secondary that complements your {{primary}}.
guidance.secondaryTheory: Secondaries (orange, green, violet) come from mixing two primaries. Facing {{primary}}, choose {{options}}.
guidance.tertiarySubtitle: A tertiary shade between your primary and secondary — ideal for shadows, accents and transitions.
guidance.tertiaryTheory: Tertiaries (red-orange, yellow-green, blue-violet…) enrich the palette without overcrowding it. Think 60 % primary · 30 % secondary · 10 % tertiary.

tips.1: Use this primary for the large masses (~60 % of the surface).
tips.2: The secondary balances the primary — keep it for mid-areas (~30 %).
tips.3: The tertiary is for accents, edges and details (~10 %).

questions.1: Test the hue on a swatch strip before covering the canvas.
questions.2: Mix on the palette with a knife — not directly on the paper.
questions.3: A touch of white softens the tertiary without fully desaturating it.

synthesis.full: Primary, secondary and tertiary form a balanced painting palette (60·30·10 ratio).
synthesis.partial: Primary and secondary are enough to start — you can add a tertiary or move on to the exercise.
synthesis.single: A primary sets the base — continue to build your palette.

mirror.synthesisWithLabels: Your painting palette ({{labels}}) is ready — primary for masses, secondary for balance, tertiary for accents.
mirror.synthesisEmpty: Your palette is ready — test each hue on a swatch strip before painting.
mirror.turn: {{chosen}} ({{dim}}) joins your palette — keep the 60·30·10 ratio in mind for each role.

emotionExplorer.emotionDescription: {{quadrant}} — choose the word that comes closest to what you feel.
